content: Such co-administration is not recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of ribociclib by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism; therefore, alternative drugs should be considered, and co-administration with strong CYP3A inducers should be avoided. Similarly, rifampin decreases the levels or effects of rifabutin, rimegepant, ripretinib, ritlecitinib, ritonavir, rolapitant, romidepsin, selpercatinib, selumetinib, silodosin, simvastatin, siponimod, sirolimus, sofosbuvir, sofosbuvir/velpatasvir, solifenacin, sonidegib, sorafenib, sotagliflozin, sotorasib, sparsentan, stiripentol, sulbactam/durlobactam, sunitinib, tacrolimus, tamsulosin, tazemetostat, temsirolimus, tezacaftor, theophylline, tivozanib, tizanidine, tolterodine, tolvaptan, tovorafenib, trabectedin, trazodone, triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension, triazolam, tucatinib, typhoid vaccine live, ubrogepant, ulipristal, upadacitinib, valbenazine, vardenafil, velpatasvir, vemurafenib, venetoclax, verapamil, vonoprazan, vorapaxar, voriconazole, voxilaprevir, zanubrutinib, zavegepant intranasal, zuranolone, abiraterone, alfentanil, alfuzosin, alosetron, aluminum hydroxide, ambrisentan, amikacin, amitriptyline, amlodipine, amobarbital, antipyrine, apalutamide, armodafinil, artesunate, asenapine, atogepant, atorvastatin, atovaquone, avanafil, avatrombopag, azithromycin, bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens, belumosudil, bendamustine, benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen, berotralstat, bexagliflozin, bexarotene, bortezomib, bosentan, bosutinib, brentuximab vedotin, brexpiprazole, brivaracetam, bromocriptine, budesonide, buprenorphine (including buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, and long-acting injection forms), bupropion, butabarbital, butalbital, cabazitaxel, calcifediol, calcitriol, calcium carbonate, calcium/vitamin D, canagliflozin, cannabidiol, carvedilol, and other drugs by affecting hepatic or intestinal enzyme metabolism, particularly CYP3A4, CYP2C9, CYP2B6, CYP1A2, or P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. In many cases, co-administration with rifampin is contraindicated or requires close monitoring, therapy modification, or the use of alternative drugs. For some drugs, dose adjustments may be necessary to maintain therapeutic efficacy. For example, abiraterone dosage may need to be increased to twice daily if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Similarly, brexpiprazole and brivaracetam doses may need to be doubled when used with rifampin. For buprenorphine formulations, careful monitoring for withdrawal symptoms or overmedication is required, and alternative formulations may be necessary if CYP3A4 inducers cannot be discontinued. In cases where rifampin reduces the absorption of drugs (e.g., antacids like aluminum hydroxide or calcium carbonate), it is recommended to administer rifampin at least one hour before antacid ingestion. For drugs like atogepant, specific dosage adjustments are recommended when co-administered with OATP inhibitors.
